SOURCE: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-lifecycle-hooks.html
FETCHED: 2026-09-27  (first full audit; backlog item raised 2026-09-26)

*** LITERAL FACTS ONLY — do not replace with a prose summary. ***

CONFIGURATION
- Hooks set on CreateHarness / UpdateHarness. NOT available as an InvokeHarness override.
- Max 20 hooks per harness. Hook names unique within the harness.
- UpdateHarness `hooks` REPLACES the entire existing list. Empty list = remove all hooks.
  Omitting `hooks` retains existing config.  => single-call silent de-instrumentation.

EVENTS (4) and deny behavior
  before_invocation  ctx = ordered `messages` from the current InvokeHarness request,
                     BEFORE the harness restores session state.
                     deny => stops invocation; messageStop stopReason = "hook_stopped".
  before_tool_call   ctx = toolName, toolType, toolUseId, toolInput.
                     deny => skips the tool call; agent loop CONTINUES.
  after_tool_call    ctx = toolName, toolType, toolUseId, toolResult, error.
                     deny => KEEPS the completed tool result, then stops the invocation.
  after_invocation   ctx = stopReason, usage{inputTokens,outputTokens}.
                     deny => reported in stream only; cannot retract streamed output.

TARGETS (3)
  Lambda        synchronous RequestResponse, waits up to timeoutSeconds.
                *** ONLY target type that can change agent-loop behavior. ***
                must return {"decision":"allow"|"deny", "reason"?} ; reason capped 1024 chars.
                timeoutSeconds default 60, range 1-900.
                failureMode on timeout/error/invalid response: "deny" (default) | "allow".
                Multiple Lambda hooks on the same event run CONCURRENTLY; any deny applies;
                first denying hook in list order supplies the reason.
  SNS           publish as SNS Message. Non-blocking. NO decision returned.
                FIFO topic: message group ID derived from harness ARN + session ID.
  EventBridge   payload in `detail`, source "bedrock-agentcore.harness",
                detail-type "Harness Lifecycle Hook". Non-blocking. NO decision.
  Standard SNS and EventBridge DO NOT guarantee lifecycle event order.
  Delivery errors do NOT stop the invocation.
  Execution role needs permission per target — see harness-security.md#harness-lifecycle-hook-permissions.

*** CONTEXT TRUNCATION — 64 KiB cap per `context` object ***
  before_invocation: keeps newest contiguous complete messages that fit; adds
    "truncated": true; if newest message alone exceeds limit, `messages` = [].
  other events: harness REPLACES the largest context fields with
    {"truncated": true, "preview": "<prefix of the serialized field>"}
  *** VERBATIM: "Context truncation does not activate failureMode. The Lambda function
      receives the truncated context and must return a decision." ***
  => toolInput / toolResult are exactly the fields most likely to be replaced.

INLINE FUNCTIONS (#harness-hook-inline-functions)
  - Tool-call hooks DO run for inline_function tools. before_tool_call fires after the model
    generates the request and before handoff for CLIENT-SIDE execution.
  - VERBATIM: "The model-generated request can appear in earlier stream events before the
    hook decision; before_tool_call controls execution, not visibility in the stream."
  - Result returned in a LATER InvokeHarness request with the same runtimeSessionId.
    That follow-up is a NEW invocation => invocation hooks run again; before_tool_call is
    NOT repeated; after_tool_call runs once with the submitted result.
  - Ordering: harness tool A -> inline B (waits for result) -> harness tool C. Multiple
    inline functions handed off one at a time.
  - deny on before_tool_call B => skip B, continue to C. deny on after_tool_call B =>
    retain B's result, stop before C.
  - VERBATIM WARNING: "An after_tool_call event for an inline function confirms that the
    harness processed a result supplied by the client. It does not attest that the client
    performed the external action represented by that result. Authenticate the caller and
    validate the result before using the event as an authorization or audit signal."

RESPONSE STREAM
  InvokeHarness emits a `hookEvent` per fired hook: {hookEventId, name, type, decision, reason}.
  *** For SNS/EventBridge, `decision` and `reason` are ABSENT and the hookEvent
      "does not confirm that the target received the event." ***
  after_invocation hookEvent follows terminal messageStop; some error paths emit
  after_invocation with NO messageStop.

REPORTED 2026-09-27 as [AIDR][MEDIUM] (truncation + non-authoritative hook events).
The 4 hook points / Lambda-deny basics were already reported 2026-09-22 — do not re-report.
